column1: 1:1|These are the words of Amos, who was among the sheep breeders of Tekoa—what he saw concerning Israel during the reigns of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.|Preserves occupation, visionary description, both reigns, and earthquake interval without supplying an absolute date.

1:2|He said:
“The LORD roars from Zion
and raises his voice from Jerusalem.
The shepherds’ pastures mourn,
and the summit of Carmel dries up.”|Keeps the roar, mournful pasture, and specific mountain; matches Joel's shared formula where clear.

1:3|This is what the LORD says:
“For three rebellions of Damascus, and for four,
I will not turn it back:
they threshed Gilead with iron threshing sledges.|Preserves the cumulative number formula and open it; retains the brutal agricultural image.
1:4|I will send fire into the house of Hazael,\nand it will consume Ben-hadad’s citadels.|Keeps dynasty names and the repeated fire/citadel formula.

1:5|I will break the gate bar of Damascus,
cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven
and the scepter-holder from Beth-eden.
The people of Aram will go into exile to Kir,” says the LORD.|Retains all place-names and distinguishes inhabitant from ruler rather than silently equating both.

1:6|This is what the LORD says:
“For three rebellions of Gaza, and for four,
I will not turn it back:
they deported an entire community
to hand them over to Edom.|Preserves total deportation and transfer destination without importing modern Gaza referents.
1:7|I will send fire into Gaza’s wall,\nand it will consume her citadels.|Repeats the judgment form while retaining the city's feminine personification.

1:8|I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod
and the scepter-holder from Ashkelon.
I will turn my hand against Ekron,
and the remaining Philistines will perish,”
says the Lord GOD.|Keeps all three cities, remnant outcome, and adonai/YHWH title convention.

1:9|This is what the LORD says:
“For three rebellions of Tyre, and for four,
I will not turn it back:
they handed an entire community over to Edom
and did not remember a covenant of brothers.|Preserves deportation and covenant breach as separate charges with kinship language intact.
1:10|I will send fire into Tyre’s wall,\nand it will consume her citadels.”|Retains the refrain without unnecessary variation.

1:11|This is what the LORD says:
“For three rebellions of Edom, and for four,
I will not turn it back:
he pursued his brother with a sword
and destroyed his compassion.
His anger tore on and on;
he kept his fury forever.|Keeps fraternal violence and sustained personified anger rather than a generic hostility summary.
1:12|I will send fire into Teman,\nand it will consume Bozrah’s citadels.”|Preserves the two distinct Edomite place-names.

1:13|This is what the LORD says:
“For three rebellions of the Ammonites, and for four,
I will not turn it back:
they ripped open Gilead’s pregnant women
to enlarge their territory.|Preserves the actual atrocity and explicitly territorial motive.

1:14|I will set fire to Rabbah’s wall,
and it will consume her citadels,
amid shouts on the day of battle,
amid a whirlwind on the day of storm.|Keeps ignite distinct from send and both paired day clauses.
1:15|Their king will go into exile,\nhe and his rulers together,” says the LORD.|Follows pointed their king while noting the possible Milcom name reading.

2:1|This is what the LORD says:
“For three rebellions of Moab, and for four,
I will not turn it back:
he burned the bones of Edom’s king into lime.|Keeps the desecration of a foreign king's remains as the stated charge.

2:2|I will send fire into Moab,
and it will consume Kerioth’s citadels.
Moab will die amid uproar,
with battle cries and the sound of a ram’s horn.|Preserves the proper name and threefold battle soundscape.
2:3|I will cut off the judge from her midst\nand kill all her rulers with him,” says the LORD.|Keeps judge rather than replacing it with king and preserves all rulers.

2:4|This is what the LORD says:
“For three rebellions of Judah, and for four,
I will not turn it back:
they rejected the LORD’s instruction
and did not keep his decrees.
Their lies led them astray,
the lies their ancestors followed.|Retains instruction/decrees and lies without silently substituting idols.
2:5|I will send fire into Judah,\nand it will consume Jerusalem’s citadels.”|Keeps the fire refrain equally applied to Judah.

2:6|This is what the LORD says:
“For three rebellions of Israel, and for four,
I will not turn it back:
they sell the innocent for silver
and the needy for a pair of sandals.|Uses innocent in judicial context and retains the concrete low price rather than only saying exploitation.

2:7|They crave even the dust of the ground on the heads of the poor
and twist the path of the afflicted.
A man and his father go to the same young woman,
profaning my holy name.|Follows the difficult pant/crave wording rather than silently emending to trample; preserves sexual abuse context without calling the woman a prostitute.

2:8|They stretch out beside every altar
on clothes taken as pledges,
and in the house of their God
they drink wine taken in fines.|Connects worship to seized collateral and fines while preserving the physical scene.

2:9|Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them,
tall as cedars and strong as oaks.
I destroyed his fruit above
and his roots below.|Keeps tree similes and total above/below destruction with divine emphasis.
2:10|I brought you up from the land of Egypt\nand led you through the wilderness for forty years\nto take possession of the Amorite’s land.|Preserves forty years and the purpose of the journey.

2:11|I raised up some of your sons as prophets\nand some of your young men as Nazirites.\nIs this not so, people of Israel?” declares the LORD.|Retains male-specific groups and the Nazirite term rather than generalizing dedication.
2:12|“But you made the Nazirites drink wine\nand commanded the prophets, ‘Do not prophesy!’|Keeps the two direct violations and quoted prohibition.
2:13|Now I will press down beneath you\nas a cart loaded with sheaves presses down.|Preserves the difficult pressure image and notes alternate creaking interpretation.
2:14|The swift will have no escape;\nthe strong will find no strength;\nthe warrior will not save his life.|Keeps the three progressively defeated capacities and repeated escape theme.
2:15|The archer will not stand his ground;\nthe fleet-footed will not escape;\nthe horseman will not save his life.|Retains distinct military roles and matches the preceding survival refrain.
2:16|Even the bravest of warriors\nwill flee naked on that day,” declares the LORD.|Preserves naked flight and specified day without softening humiliation.

3:1|Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, people of Israel—against the whole family I brought up from the land of Egypt:|Retains the sudden first-person divine quotation inside the introductory address.

3:2|“You alone have I known
among all the families of the earth.
That is why I will call you to account
for all your guilt.”|Preserves knowing as relationship and the surprising accountability consequence of election.
3:3|Do two people walk together\nunless they have arranged to meet?|Renders noadu as meeting rather than broad ideological agreement.
3:4|Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey?\nDoes a young lion cry from its den\nunless it has caught something?|Keeps both causally linked animal questions without explanatory answers.

3:5|Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground
unless a snare is set for it?
Does a trap spring up from the ground
without catching anything?|Retains two trap mechanisms as rhetorical cause/effect questions.

3:6|When a ram’s horn sounds in a city,
do the people not tremble?
When disaster strikes a city,
has the LORD not brought it about?|Preserves the direct divine-agency claim while distinguishing disaster from moral evil.
3:7|The Lord GOD does nothing\nwithout revealing his counsel\nto his servants the prophets.|Keeps the counsel/servants relationship and does not expand it into a modern universal prediction rule.
3:8|A lion has roared—who will not fear?\nThe Lord GOD has spoken—who will not prophesy?|Maintains the climactic paired questions and returns to the opening roar.

3:9|Proclaim to the citadels of Ashdod
and the citadels in the land of Egypt:
“Gather on Samaria’s mountains
and see the great turmoil within her
and the oppression in her midst.”|Follows pinned Ashdod and summons foreign observers to the city's violence.
3:10|“They do not know how to do right,” declares the LORD,\n“those who store up violence and plunder in their citadels.”|Keeps the ironic stored wealth of violence and the knowledge diagnosis.

3:11|So this is what the Lord GOD says:
“An enemy will surround the land,
pull down your strength,
and plunder your citadels.”|Supplies a verb for the terse encircling enemy and preserves address to personified city.

3:12|This is what the LORD says:
“As a shepherd rescues from a lion’s mouth
two leg bones or a scrap of ear,
so will the people of Israel be rescued—
those who sit in Samaria
on a corner of a bed and on a Damascus couch.”|Preserves the ironic minimal rescue and difficult Damascus couch phrase rather than inventing secure escape.
3:13|“Hear and testify against the house of Jacob,”\ndeclares the Lord GOD, the God of Armies.|Retains all divine titles and courtroom witness command.

3:14|“On the day I call Israel to account for his rebellions,
I will also call Bethel’s altars to account.
The altar’s horns will be cut off
and fall to the ground.|Keeps the repeated accountability verb and concrete altar horns.

3:15|I will strike the winter house together with the summer house.\nThe ivory houses will perish,\nand many houses will come to an end,” declares the LORD.|Preserves seasonal luxury residences and ivory without claiming solid-ivory construction.

4:1|Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on Samaria’s mountain,\nyou women who oppress the poor and crush the needy,\nwho say to your husbands, ‘Bring us something to drink!’|Makes the feminine addressees clear while retaining the harsh cattle insult and exploitation.

4:2|The Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness:
“Days are coming upon you
when you will be carried away with hooks,
the last of you with fishhooks.|Preserves oath, captivity, and both hook terms; alternative containers noted.

4:3|You will go out through breaches in the wall,\neach woman straight ahead,\nand you will be flung toward Harmon,” declares the LORD.|Keeps individual female captives and the uncertain destination rather than replacing it with a known location.

4:4|“Go to Bethel and rebel!
Go to Gilgal and multiply rebellion!
Bring your sacrifices every morning
and your tithes every three days.|Retains the sarcasm and literal three days rather than harmonizing to legal three-year tithes.

4:5|Burn a thank offering of leavened bread;
proclaim freewill offerings—announce them!
For that is what you love, people of Israel,”
declares the Lord GOD.|Keeps leavened offering and ostentatious proclamation without smoothing the irony.

4:6|“I gave you clean teeth in all your cities\nand no bread in any of your settlements.\nYet you did not return to me,” declares the LORD.|Preserves clean-teeth famine idiom and the exact refrain to recur five times.

4:7|“I also withheld rain from you
when harvest was still three months away.
I sent rain on one city but not another.
One field received rain;
the field without rain dried up.|Retains the three-month interval and unequal local rainfall rather than general drought alone.

4:8|People from two or three cities staggered to one city for water,\nbut they could not drink their fill.\nYet you did not return to me,” declares the LORD.|Preserves city numbers, exhausted movement, and unchanged refrain.

4:9|“I struck you with blight and mildew.
The cutting locust ate your many gardens and vineyards,
your fig trees and olive trees.
Yet you did not return to me,” declares the LORD.|Keeps all crops and two crop diseases; matches gazam terminology used in Joel.

4:10|“I sent pestilence among you as in Egypt.
I killed your young men with the sword,
and your horses were captured.
I made the stench of your camps rise into your nostrils.
Yet you did not return to me,” declares the LORD.|Retains death, capture, and corpse stench rather than sanitizing the judgment.

4:11|“I overthrew some of you
as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
You were like a charred stick snatched from a fire.
Yet you did not return to me,” declares the LORD.|Preserves third-person God inside divine speech and the narrow-rescue image.

4:12|“So this is what I will do to you, Israel.\nBecause I will do this to you,\nprepare to meet your God, Israel!”|Keeps this unexplained, as in the source, rather than inventing the threatened action.

4:13|Look: he forms the mountains and creates the wind;
he tells human beings what his thought is.
He turns dawn to darkness
and treads the heights of the earth.
The LORD, the God of Armies, is his name.|Retains creation, disclosure, darkness, and heights; notes ambiguity of whose thought is disclosed.
5:1|Hear this word I take up over you\nas a funeral lament, house of Israel:|Signals the literary form explicitly using qinah's funeral sense.

5:2|“Fallen is virgin Israel, never to rise again.\nAbandoned on her own ground,\nshe has no one to raise her.”|Preserves feminine national personification and the unqualified lament before later hope.

5:3|For this is what the Lord GOD says:
“The city that marches out a thousand
will have a hundred left;
the one that marches out a hundred
will have ten left for the house of Israel.”|Keeps exact thousand/hundred/ten attrition and military movement.
5:4|For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel:\n“Seek me and live.|Retains the concise imperative linking seeking and life.

5:5|Do not seek Bethel;
do not go to Gilgal
or cross over to Beer-sheba.
Gilgal will certainly go into exile,
and Bethel will become nothing.”|Preserves all three pilgrimage sites and Gilgal/exile, Bethel/worthlessness wordplay through a note.

5:6|Seek the LORD and live,
or he may sweep through the house of Joseph like fire
and consume it,
with no one at Bethel to put it out.|Keeps the third-person exhortation and Bethel reference rather than substituting Israel.
5:7|You turn justice into wormwood\nand throw righteousness to the ground!|Retains the bitter plant and discarded righteousness as concrete images.

5:8|He made the Pleiades and Orion.
He turns deep darkness into morning
and darkens day into night.
He calls for the sea’s waters
and pours them over the earth’s surface.
The LORD is his name.|Keeps both star groups, opposed light transformations, and waters without supplying a mechanism.
5:9|He flashes devastation upon the strong,\nand devastation comes upon the fortress.|Retains repeated devastation and suddenness of the rare verb.
5:10|They hate the one who rebukes at the gate\nand detest the one who speaks honestly.|Keeps gate as legal setting and the two forms of truthful speech.

5:11|Because you trample the poor
and take levies of grain from them,
you have built houses of dressed stone,
but you will not live in them.
You have planted lovely vineyards,
but you will not drink their wine.|Preserves exploitation, luxury construction, and two frustrated enjoyments.

5:12|I know how many your rebellions are,
how enormous your sins—
you who harass the innocent, accept bribes,
and turn the needy away at the gate.|Makes the three judicial abuses clear while keeping the gate image.
5:13|That is why the prudent keep silent at such a time,\nfor it is an evil time.|States the observation without adding approval of silence.

5:14|Seek good, not evil, so that you may live.\nThen the LORD, the God of Armies, will be with you,\nas you claim he is.|Preserves the challenge to claimed divine presence rather than treating it as an unconditional assurance.

5:15|Hate evil, love good,
and establish justice at the gate.
Perhaps the LORD, the God of Armies,
will show favor to the remnant of Joseph.|Retains perhaps and the remnant limitation rather than promising automatic pardon.

5:16|So this is what the Lord, the LORD, the God of Armies, says:
“In every square there will be lamentation;
in every street they will cry, ‘Alas! Alas!’
They will call farmers to mourning
and skilled mourners to lament.|Preserves the full title sequence and both ordinary and professional mourners.
5:17|There will be lamentation in every vineyard,\nfor I will pass through your midst,” says the LORD.|Keeps divine passing-through and reversal of vineyard joy.
5:18|Woe to you who long for the day of the LORD!\nWhat will the day of the LORD mean for you?\nIt will be darkness, not light.|Retains two name occurrences and the reversal of desired expectations.

5:19|It will be like a man fleeing a lion
only to meet a bear,
or going home, resting his hand on the wall,
and being bitten by a snake.|Preserves the sequential failed escapes and ordinary gesture at home.
5:20|Will not the day of the LORD be darkness, not light—\ngloom without a ray of brightness?|Keeps the repeated question rather than collapsing it into v18.
5:21|“I hate, I reject your festivals;\nI will not savor your solemn assemblies.|Retains two rejection verbs and the smell/savor metaphor.

5:22|Even if you offer me burnt offerings and grain offerings,\nI will not accept them.\nI will not look upon your fellowship offerings of fattened animals.|Keeps the three offering types and successive sensory rejection.
5:23|Take the noise of your songs away from me!\nI will not listen to the music of your harps.|Preserves the harsh noise designation and refusal to hear.

5:24|Let justice roll like water,\nand righteousness like a stream that never runs dry.|Retains familiar clear wording and explains perennial strength through natural English, without novelty for its own sake.

5:25|Did you bring me sacrifices and grain offerings\nduring the forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?|Preserves the difficult historical question without resolving its expected answer in the verse.

5:26|You will carry Sikkuth your king\nand Kiyyun your images,\nthe star of your god that you made for yourselves.|Follows pinned names and future exile linkage; notes tense and ancient version alternatives.
5:27|I will send you into exile beyond Damascus,”\nsays the LORD, whose name is the God of Armies.|Retains Damascus rather than harmonizing to a later quotation's Babylon.

6:1|Woe to those at ease in Zion
and those secure on Samaria’s mountain—
the renowned men of the foremost nation,
to whom the house of Israel comes!|Preserves both capitals and elite self-positioning without limiting the oracle to one city.

6:2|Cross over to Calneh and look;
go from there to great Hamath,
then down to Gath of the Philistines.
Are they better than these kingdoms?
Is their territory larger than yours?|Keeps the comparison's ambiguous pronouns and all three places.
6:3|You push the evil day far away\nwhile bringing the reign of violence near.|Preserves the far/near antithesis and violence's seat/rule image.

6:4|You lie on ivory beds
and sprawl on couches,
eating lambs from the flock
and calves from the stall.|Keeps physical luxury, posture, and selected meat without adding modern class terminology.
6:5|You improvise to the sound of the harp\nand invent musical instruments for yourselves like David.|Retains David comparison and creative music rather than inserting irony into the wording.
6:6|You drink wine from bowls\nand anoint yourselves with the finest oils,\nbut you do not grieve over Joseph’s ruin.|Preserves excess vessels and oil against the ungrieved collective wound.
6:7|So now you will lead the way into exile,\nand the revelry of those who sprawl will end.|Keeps the first-in-status to first-in-exile reversal and repeats sprawling.

6:8|The Lord GOD has sworn by himself,
declares the LORD, the God of Armies:
“I detest Jacob’s pride and hate his citadels.
I will hand over the city and everything in it.”|Preserves oath and both divine-name occurrences with titles intact.
6:9|If ten men remain in one house, they too will die.|Keeps the precise ten and total survival reversal.

6:10|When a man’s relative, the one who burns the body, carries out the bones, he will ask someone in the back of the house, “Is anyone else with you?” The answer will be, “No one.” Then he will say, “Hush! We must not mention the name of the LORD.”|Preserves the difficult body-burner term, exchange, and unexplained prohibition rather than inventing ritual background.
6:11|For look: the LORD gives the command,\nand the great house is smashed to pieces,\nthe small house split apart.|Keeps both house sizes and distinct destruction images.

6:12|Do horses run on rock?
Does anyone plow it with oxen?
Yet you have turned justice into poison
and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.|Follows pinned oxen rather than redividing into sea; retains absurdity and poisoned fruit.
6:13|You rejoice over Lo-debar\nand say, “Did we not capture Karnaim by our own strength?”|Retains place-names whose meanings nothing/horns carry the boast's irony; explains in note.

6:14|“Look, house of Israel, I am raising a nation against you,”
declares the LORD, the God of Armies.
“They will oppress you from Lebo-hamath
to the Wadi of the Arabah.”|Keeps unnamed invader and both territorial endpoints.

7:1|This is what the Lord GOD showed me: he was forming a swarm of locusts just as the late crop began to grow—the crop after the king’s mowing.|Preserves timing relative to royal harvest without inventing a tax percentage.

7:2|When they had finished eating the land’s vegetation, I said, “Lord GOD, please forgive! How can Jacob stand? He is so small.”|Keeps the prophet's intercession and weakness argument rather than an innocence claim.
7:3|The LORD relented about this. “It will not happen,” the LORD said.|Retains both name occurrences and explicit relenting.

7:4|This is what the Lord GOD showed me: the Lord GOD was calling for judgment by fire. It consumed the great deep and was consuming the land.|Preserves repeated title, cosmic deep, and the fire reaching the allotted portion.
7:5|I said, “Lord GOD, please stop! How can Jacob stand? He is so small.”|Distinguishes stop from earlier forgive while repeating the appeal exactly.
7:6|The LORD relented about this. “This too will not happen,” the Lord GOD said.|Keeps too and title difference from the first response.

7:7|This is what he showed me: the Lord was standing beside a wall built with a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.|Uses traditional plumb-line reading for uncertain anak, explicitly noted rather than claimed certain.

7:8|The LORD asked me, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “A plumb line.” The Lord said, “I am setting a plumb line among my people Israel. I will no longer pass them by.|Preserves the question-answer sequence and distinction LORD/Lord.

7:9|Isaac’s high places will be desolate,\nand Israel’s sanctuaries laid waste.\nI will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”|Keeps Isaac's uncommon spelling/name and dynasty rather than king alone.

7:10|Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel: “Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land cannot bear all his words.|Keeps accusation as Amaziah's report, not narrator's judgment.

7:11|For this is what Amos says: ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will certainly go into exile away from its land.’”|Preserves the report's king/dynasty difference from v9 instead of harmonizing quotations.
7:12|Amaziah told Amos, “Seer, go! Flee to the land of Judah. Earn your bread there, and prophesy there.|Makes the bread-as-livelihood idiom readable while retaining seer as distinct term.
7:13|But do not prophesy at Bethel anymore. It is the king’s sanctuary, the kingdom’s temple.”|Preserves the political ownership claim and two designations.

7:14|Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet, nor a prophet’s son. I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.|Chooses past tense in context but notes Hebrew verbless present alternative and guild sense of son.

7:15|But the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD told me, ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’|Retains both divine names and direct commissioning against professional livelihood framing.

7:16|Now hear the word of the LORD. You say, ‘Do not prophesy against Israel; do not pour out words against the house of Isaac.’|Preserves the dripping/pouring speech image without making it literal rain.

7:17|So this is what the LORD says: ‘Your wife will become a prostitute in the city; your sons and daughters will fall by the sword; your land will be divided by a measuring line. You will die on unclean ground, and Israel will certainly go into exile away from its land.’”|Retains the full family catastrophe and ritual uncleanness without attributing voluntary choice to the wife.
8:1|This is what the Lord GOD showed me: a basket of summer fruit.|Keeps the visual object that grounds the coming wordplay.

8:2|He asked, “What do you see, Amos?” I answered, “A basket of summer fruit.” Then the LORD said to me, “The end has come for my people Israel. I will no longer pass them by.|Retains summer fruit/end wordplay in its actual nouns, explained in note, and repeats the earlier no-passing declaration.
8:3|The temple songs will turn to wailing on that day,” declares the Lord GOD. “So many bodies, thrown everywhere! Hush!”|Preserves abrupt corpse fragments and hush; temple/palace alternative noted.
8:4|Hear this, you who pant after the needy\nto make the poor of the land cease to exist,|Keeps the predatory panting root and explicit destructive purpose.

8:5|saying, “When will the new moon be over so we can sell grain,
and the Sabbath, so we can open the grain bins?
We will shrink the ephah, increase the shekel,
and cheat with crooked scales.|Preserves holy-day impatience and each fraudulent measurement mechanism.
8:6|We will buy the poor for silver\nand the needy for a pair of sandals,\nand even sell the grain sweepings.”|Repeats the sandals motif and keeps sale of inferior remnants concrete.
8:7|The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob:\n“I will never forget any of their deeds.|Preserves the ambiguous oath object instead of replacing pride with a chosen referent.

8:8|Will not the land shake for this,
and everyone living in it mourn?
The whole land will rise like the Nile,
toss and sink like Egypt’s Nile.|Follows read sink and preserves river motion as earthquake imagery.
8:9|On that day,” declares the Lord GOD,\n“I will make the sun go down at noon\nand darken the earth in broad daylight.|Keeps noon and daylight without identifying a historical eclipse.

8:10|I will turn your festivals into mourning
and all your songs into funeral laments.
I will put sackcloth on every waist
and baldness on every head.
I will make it like mourning for an only child,
and its end like a bitter day.|Preserves all mourning practices and only-child comparison.

8:11|Days are coming,” declares the Lord GOD,
“when I will send a famine through the land—
not hunger for bread or thirst for water,
but for hearing the words of the LORD.|Retains the shift from physical scarcity to lack of hearing, not lack of written books.

8:12|They will stagger from sea to sea,
from north to east.
They will roam in search of the word of the LORD
but will not find it.|Keeps the unusual directional pair rather than filling all compass points.
8:13|On that day beautiful young women\nand young men will faint from thirst.|Preserves both groups and physical fainting.

8:14|Those who swear by Samaria’s Guilt,
who say, ‘As your god lives, Dan!’
and ‘As the way of Beer-sheba lives!’—
they will fall and never rise again.”|Retains the difficult Guilt and way oath objects, with deity-name alternatives in note.

9:1|I saw the Lord standing beside the altar. He said:
“Strike the capital so the thresholds shake;
bring them down on everyone’s heads.
Those who remain I will kill with the sword.
No fugitive will get away; no escapee will survive.|Keeps the violent sanctuary collapse and both repeated no-escape assertions.

9:2|Even if they dig into Sheol,
my hand will take them from there.
Even if they climb to heaven,
I will bring them down from there.|Preserves cosmological extremes and repeated from there.

9:3|Even if they hide on Carmel’s summit,
I will search them out and take them from there.
Even if they conceal themselves from my eyes on the seabed,
I will command the serpent there to bite them.|Keeps mountain/deep-sea contrast and unnamed serpent without modern zoological identification.

9:4|Even if they go into captivity before their enemies,\nI will command the sword there to kill them.\nI will set my eyes upon them for harm, not for good.”|Preserves captivity as no refuge and the reversal of divine watchfulness.

9:5|The Lord GOD of Armies
touches the earth, and it melts;
everyone living in it mourns.
The whole earth rises like the Nile
and sinks like Egypt’s Nile.|Keeps melt and mourning with the repeated Nile motion.

9:6|He builds his upper chambers in the heavens
and founds his vault upon the earth.
He calls for the sea’s waters
and pours them over the earth’s surface.
The LORD is his name.|Retains ancient architectural cosmology and repeats the water formula.

9:7|“Are you not like the Cushites to me, people of Israel?”
declares the LORD.
“Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt,
the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?|Keeps all three migrations and the Cushite comparison without reducing it to a modern racial argument.

9:8|Look, the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom,
and I will destroy it from the face of the ground.
Yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,”
declares the LORD.|Preserves distinction between kingdom destroyed and house not totally destroyed.

9:9|“I will give the command
and shake the house of Israel among all the nations
as something is shaken in a sieve,
without a pebble falling to the ground.|Follows pebble for tseror rather than substituting grain and flags the image's interpretive implications.
9:10|All the sinners among my people will die by the sword—\nthose who say, ‘Disaster will never approach or overtake us.’|Keeps the specified boast and limits all to sinners among the people.

9:11|On that day I will raise David’s fallen shelter,\nrepair its breaches, raise its ruins,\nand rebuild it as in ancient days,|Retains shelter rather than silently palace and the three restorative actions.
